steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Power: the ability to make others do what you want. Lukes identified three dimensions: decision-making, agenda-setting, and ideological power.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Weber's three types of authority: Traditional (custom - monarchy), Charismatic (personal qualities - MLK), Rational-legal (rules and laws - elected officials). Most modern authority is rational-legal.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The state: institutions that govern (government, parliament, police, courts). Marxists: the state serves ruling class interests. Functionalists: the state serves collective interests. Pluralists: the state balances competing interests.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Power elites: Mills argued power is concentrated in a small group of corporate leaders, military chiefs and politicians. In the UK, the 'establishment' (Eton, Oxbridge) dominates politics, media and business.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe Weber's three types of authority and evaluate their usefulness. | Compare Marxist and Functionalist views of the state. | Evaluate whether democracy ensures that power is equally distributed.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Weber's 3 types: Traditional (custom), Charismatic (personality), Rational-legal (rules). Marxist: state = tool of ruling class. Functionalist: state = serves everyone. Democracy = formal equality but REAL power is unequal (money, media, lobbying).
